objectives.objective: Obtain RCE on the DVWA web application pod
Establish persistence with a ReaperC2 beacon
Obtain root on the webapp pod (blocked - no compatible kernel LPE)
Get host-level execution access (blocked - hardened container + patched kernel)

scope.name: DVWA web app (http://10.0.20.75:30280/)
scope.description_rt: Exposed NodePort; command injection, authentication bypass, and post-exploitation of the hosting pod.

scope.description_rt: Worker node k8s-worker1 (10.0.20.75), kubelet, pod service account, and node kernel as test infra with snapshots.

whitecards.title: kubectl access to test cluster
whitecards.description: Operator provided cluster-admin kubectl for pod/node recovery (test infra only)

findings.title: DVWA Command Injection - Remote Code Execution
findings.affected_entities_rt: DVWA pod (dvwa-78d998d9bd-*) on k8s-worker1, exposed at http://10.0.20.75:30280/.
findings.description_rt: The /vulnerabilities/exec/ endpoint of DVWA at security level "low" passes the user-supplied ip parameter unsanitized to PHP shell_exec, allowing shell metacharacter injection. A payload of the form 127.0.0.1; <command> executes arbitrary commands as the web-server user.
findings.impact_rt: Unauthenticated-to-RCE on the application pod, enabling full compromise of the pod, deployment of persistent C2, and a launch point for in-cluster movement and kernel-level privilege escalation against the host node.
findings.replication_steps_rt: Authenticate to DVWA (admin/password), set security level to "low", POST ip=127.0.0.1; id&Submit=Submit to /vulnerabilities/exec/; observe uid=33(www-data) in the <pre> response block.
findings.host_detection_techniques_rt: Alert on sh/bash/shell_exec child processes of the Apache/PHP-FPM worker; alert on outbound curl/wget from the www-data user; web WAF rule for ; | && $( backtick metacharacters in the ip parameter.
findings.recommendation_rt: Never expose DVWA outside isolated training environments. Where required, set security level to "impossible" (prepared statements + escapeshellarg), enforce non-default credentials, and front with a WAF.

findings.title: DVWA Default / Weak Credentials
findings.description_rt: DVWA shipped with the default admin / password credential pair, which the operator used as the assumed-breach starting point. Default credentials are a trivial first step for any adversary once the application is reachable.
findings.impact_rt: Direct authentication bypass, removing the only barrier between an external attacker and the command-injection flaw.
findings.replication_steps_rt: Browse to /login.php, submit admin/password; observe redirect to index.php.
findings.host_detection_techniques_rt: Alert on successful login using the known default admin credential from an external source IP; periodic credential audit.
findings.recommendation_rt: Enforce non-default, strong credentials on first deploy; remove default accounts; add MFA where the application supports it.

findings.title: Excessive Linux Capabilities and Disabled seccomp on Application Pod
findings.description_rt: The pod ran with PID 1 effective capabilities 0xa80425fb including CAP_SETUID, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_SYS_CHROOT, and CAP_MKNOD, with seccomp disabled and user namespaces enabled. The www-data shell retained the full bounding set (caps droppable but not gained without a SUID/file-cap binary).
findings.impact_rt: These capabilities are prerequisites for the kernel-LPE techniques attempted (raw sockets, user+net namespace creation, FIB rule manipulation) and for potential device-node-based host-disk access. They materially widened the post-RCE blast radius.
findings.replication_steps_rt: From RCE, run grep Cap /proc/1/status (shows CapEff: 00000000a80425fb) and cat /proc/self/status | grep Cap (shows CapEff: 0, CapBnd: 00000000a80425fb).
findings.host_detection_techniques_rt: Audit pod security context at admission (OPA/Kyverno policy denying broad caps and seccomp=Unconfined); alert on unshare/clone with namespace flags from container processes.
findings.recommendation_rt: Drop all capabilities, set seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault, runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true; remove CAP_NET_RAW/CAP_MKNOD/CAP_SYS_CHROOT/CAP_SETUID.

findings.title: Unpatched Kernel - Exploitable CVEs Present (CVE-2026-74581, CVE-2026-64560)
findings.description_rt: The node kernel (5.15.0-191, built Aug 7 2026) is vulnerable to CVE-2026-74581 (IPv6 FIB rule UAF, fixed 5.15.216) and CVE-2026-64560 (posix-cpu-timers UAF, fixed 5.15.213). The KASLR protection was demonstrably defeated against CVE-2026-74581 (kernel base leaked: 0xffffffff9e600000).
findings.impact_rt: A working kernel LPE (once a compatible exploit exists) would allow container escape to host root. The KASLR leak proves the protection is bypassable on this build.
findings.replication_steps_rt: From pod RCE, run the CVE-2026-74581 PoC --leak-only/leak stage; observe leaked KASLR base. Run the CVE-2026-64560 trigger --check; observe prerequisites OK.
findings.host_detection_techniques_rt: Kernel-patch compliance scan; alert on unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET) + RTM_NEWRULE/FIB rule churn from containers; anomalous timer_create/timer_delete storm.
findings.recommendation_rt: Patch kernel to >= 5.15.216; enable live-patching / rolling node updates.

findings.title: Kubelet API Reachable from Pod (anonymous auth correctly disabled)
findings.description_rt: The kubelet API (:10250) was network-reachable from inside the pod but correctly returned Unauthorized for anonymous requests and Forbidden for the pod's default service-account token (nodes/proxy denied by webhook). This is the expected secure configuration; recorded for completeness.
findings.impact_rt: None directly; confirms the kubelet authn/authz boundary held.
findings.replication_steps_rt: curl -sk https://10.0.20.75:10250/pods -> Unauthorized; with SA bearer -> Forbidden (... verb=get, resource=nodes, subresource=[proxy]).
findings.host_detection_techniques_rt: Monitor kubelet audit logs for anonymous/bearer denials; ensure --anonymous-auth=false remains set.
findings.recommendation_rt: No change required; maintain current kubelet auth settings. Optionally restrict :10250 at the network policy layer to control-plane components only.

attack_narrative.step: Critical Step 1 - Reconnaissance and Initial Access via DVWA Command Injection
attack_narrative.techniques: T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application; T1059.004 Unix Shell
attack_narrative.narrative: DVWA reachable on http://10.0.20.75:30280/. Using default credentials, authenticated and set security level to low. The /vulnerabilities/exec/ endpoint accepted an ip parameter with no input sanitization, allowing metacharacter injection. A payload 127.0.0.1; <command> was processed by PHP shell_exec, yielding remote code execution as www-data (uid 33) on the application pod (dvwa-78d998d9bd-*).

attack_narrative.step: Critical Step 2 - Persistence: ReaperC2 Beacon Delivery and C2 Establishment
attack_narrative.techniques: T1071.001 Web Protocols; T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer; T1573.002 Asymmetric Cryptography
attack_narrative.narrative: A ReaperC2 beacon binary (dvwa-parent.bin, ~10 MB) was staged on 10.0.20.243:8000 and pulled into the pod with curl to /dev/shm/dvwa-parent.bin, made executable, and launched with TERM_HARVEST=9. The beacon established an HTTPS C2 channel to metrics.harvestrangelabs.com, polling every 30 seconds. ReaperC2 registered the beacon with ClientId a6e02d08-f2b9-4641-ac1f-a292e1a8f616; the beacon log confirmed status:ok and Active:true responses, and a SOCKS5 proxy listener on :8181. The beacon survived a pod restart by being re-delivered (not reboot-persistent since /dev/shm is wiped on pod restart).

attack_narrative.step: Critical Step 3 - Discovery: Container, Kubernetes, and Privilege-Escalation Surface
attack_narrative.techniques: T1082 System Information Discovery; T1613 Container and Resource Discovery
attack_narrative.narrative: From the www-data shell, enumerated the environment: kernel 5.15.0-191-generic; seccomp disabled; user namespaces enabled; PID 1 CapEff=0xa80425fb (CAP_SETUID, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_SYS_CHROOT, CAP_MKNOD) while the www-data shell had CapEff=0 with the same bounding set; SUID set limited to standard Debian binaries with no pkexec/sudo and no file-capability binaries; /etc/passwd 644, /etc/shadow 640 root:shadow; no useful cron; no writable root-owned paths. Kubernetes: pod used the default service account (system:serviceaccount:dvwa:default) with no RBAC; kubelet :10250 reachable but webhook-denied nodes/proxy; no cloud metadata endpoint responded.

attack_narrative.step: Critical Step 4 - Privilege Escalation: Kernel LPE Attempts (Not Achieved)
attack_narrative.techniques: T1068.001 Kernel Exploitation (attempted, unsuccessful); T1611 Escape to Host (attempted, unsuccessful)
attack_narrative.narrative: Two kernel LPE attempts against 5.15.0-191-generic: (1) CVE-2026-74581 (IPv6 FIB rule UAF, fixed 5.15.216) confirmed present; KASLR defeated (base 0xffffffff9e600000, slide 0x1d600000); the only public full PoC (NebuSec/CyberMeowfia) is hardcoded for Debian 6.12.101 - its ROP gadgets, CPU-Entry-Area physical offset (CPU1_CEA_PHYS_OFFSET), and core_pattern mode-field offset are 6.12-specific; on 5.15 the post-leak pivot targets the wrong physical page, causing a kernel panic that took k8s-worker1 down twice. The blocker is CPU1_CEA_PHYS_OFFSET: a runtime, per-boot physical address not statically derivable, with no runtime leak in the exploit. Abandoned. (2) CVE-2026-64560 (posix-cpu-timers UAF, fixed 5.15.213) confirmed reachable (--check passed as www-data); no public full exploit (trigger only). Standard privesc paths exhausted with no viable route. Root on the pod and host-level execution were not achieved.

observations_and_recommendations.observation: Unsanitized Command Injection in Exposed Web Application
observations_and_recommendations.recommendation: Remove the DVWA NodePort exposure beyond the training environment. Where DVWA must be exposed, enforce the "impossible" security level, place it behind a WAF with command-injection signatures, and require non-default credentials. Never deploy DVWA on shared or production-adjacent clusters.
observations_and_recommendations.validation: ART-T1059.004-dvwa-cmdi: send ip=127.0.0.1; id to /vulnerabilities/exec/ at security level low; expected uid=33(www-data) in the <pre> block. Detection: alert on shell_exec//bin/sh -c spawned by www-data as a child of the PHP/Apache worker, and on outbound curl to non-allowlisted hosts from the pod.

observations_and_recommendations.observation: Excessive Container Capabilities and Disabled seccomp
observations_and_recommendations.recommendation: Drop all Linux capabilities except the minimum required; enable seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault (or a custom profile denying unshare, clone with CLONE_NEWUSER/NEWNET, raw sockets); set runAsNonRoot: true with a fixed non-root UID; set readOnlyRootFilesystem: true; remove CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_MKNOD, CAP_SYS_CHROOT, CAP_SETUID from the pod spec.
observations_and_recommendations.validation: ART-T1611-cap-surface: from inside the pod run grep Cap /proc/1/status and cat /proc/self/status | grep Cap; expected after remediation: CapEff: 0 for PID 1 and CapBnd reduced to only required caps, and unshare -Urn to fail under the seccomp profile.

observations_and_recommendations.recommendation: Patch the node kernel to at least 5.15.216 (fixes CVE-2026-74581) and preferably 5.15.213+ (fixes CVE-2026-64560). Enable a kernel live-patching pipeline or scheduled node rolling-updates. Keep KASLR on and add kernel hardening (page_alloc.shuffle=1, slab freelist randomization).
observations_and_recommendations.validation: ART-T1068.001-kernel-version: uname -r on the node; expected >= 5.15.216. Re-run the CVE-2026-74581 KASLR-leak trigger and confirm it no longer leaks a stable base on patched kernels.

observations_and_recommendations.observation: Unrestricted Pod Egress Enabled Beacon C2
observations_and_recommendations.recommendation: Apply a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy restricting pod egress to only required destinations/ports; block arbitrary outbound to the beacon C2 domain and to internal staging hosts.
observations_and_recommendations.validation: ART-T1071.001-beacon-egress: attempt a beacon check-in to metrics.harvestrangelabs.com from the pod; expected after remediation: the connection is denied by the NetworkPolicy and logged by the CNI (Calico) flow logs.

T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application; T1078.001 - Valid Accounts: Default Accounts

(live C2 process foothold; not autostart-persistent - see Critical Step 2)
T1068.001 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation: Kernel (attempted, unsuccessful); T1611 - Escape to Host (attempted, unsuccessful)

timeline.attack_simulation:
T+00:00 Reconnaissance: DVWA NodePort 30280 confirmed reachable (HTTP 200).
T+00:02 Initial Access: authenticated with admin/password; set security=low.
T+00:04 Execution: command injection via /vulnerabilities/exec/ -> RCE as www-data.
T+00:08 Persistence: dvwa-parent.bin delivered to /dev/shm, beacon C2 established.
T+00:15 Discovery: enumerated kernel/caps/SUID/cron/K8s SA/kubelet/metadata.
T+00:25 Privilege Escalation: CVE-2026-74581 KASLR leak succeeded (base 0xffffffff9e600000).
T+00:30 Privilege Escalation: CVE-2026-74581 pivot -> kernel panic #1 (k8s-worker1 NotReady).
T+01:00 (Node recovered via kubectl; pod rescheduled.)
T+01:05 Privilege Escalation: CVE-2026-74581 retry -> kernel panic #2.
T+01:30 (Node recovered; DVWA DB re-initialized.)
T+01:35 Persistence: beacon re-delivered, re-established (ClientId a6e02d08...).
T+01:40 Privilege Escalation: CVE-2026-64560 trigger --check passed (vuln confirmed reachable).
T+01:45 Decision: no compatible 5.15 full LPE PoC; root/host escalation not achievable.

conclusion: The engagement successfully demonstrated the Get In and Stay In phases: an external adversary with the application's default credentials could obtain remote code execution on the DVWA application pod within minutes and establish a persistent, ReaperC2-controlled HTTPS C2 foothold that maintained a live session and re-established itself after a pod restart. The beacon (ClientId a6e02d08-f2b9-4641-ac1f-a292e1a8f616) remained active throughout. The Act phase (privilege escalation to root-on-pod or host-level execution) was not achieved. The container was hardened where it matters most: the Kubernetes service account was the unprivileged default SA with no RBAC, the kubelet correctly denied anonymous and bearer-token proxy access, no cloud metadata was exposed, and the standard local-privilege-escalation surface was clean. The only remaining avenue was a kernel LPE, and the node kernel (5.15.0-191-generic) - while confirmed vulnerable to CVE-2026-74581 and CVE-2026-64560 - had no public exploit compatible with this build: the sole full PoC for CVE-2026-74581 is hardcoded for Debian 6.12.101, and its CPU-Entry-Area physical-offset pivot cannot be statically ported to 5.15 (it is a runtime, per-boot value with no runtime leak in the exploit). Defeating KASLR alone was demonstrated, proving the protection is bypassable, but a complete root-shell chain was not attainable with publicly available tooling within the engagement. An external threat could realistically replicate the RCE-and-persistence path (low skill barrier); the kernel-escape path requires advanced, target-specific exploit development and is not currently achievable with public tooling - but the presence of unpatched, exploitable kernel CVEs and the excessive container capability set mean this boundary should not be relied upon. Overall, the Get In / Stay In posture is weak and should be remediated per the observations; the Act boundary held during this engagement, but primarily due to kernel-patch and exploit-availability luck rather than defense-in-depth - patching the kernel to 5.15.216+ and tightening the pod security context are the highest-priority improvements.
